capabilities.evidence: CrossNetworkConnectPane + TransferLinkPane over one authenticated link/1 (macOS composes no legacy realtime transport as of this batch; the pairing room terminates a non-link/1 peer as unsupported); browser/native E2E coverage

on macOS a conversation is a LANE of the unified link/1 rather than a session of its own: TransferLinkPane's composer and transcript over the link's text lane, started from whichever connection method the user picked. The legacy text session and its two views are deleted from this target; RealtimeTextFrameTests/RealtimeTextSessionModelTests still cover the wire interop, consent gating and history limits of the text/1 lane the paused iOS build and the CLI still ship

Send: one shared expandSelection/SelectionStore behind all three send flows (DirectPane pairing code, NearbyPane same-network, UploadPane cloud). Folders recurse depth-first in a deterministic, locale-independent UTF-8 order, the selected folder's own name is kept, and MAX_FILES, the per-path byte bound and the sealed-BATCH-frame size are all enforced BEFORE a connection is opened or an upload starts. Symlinks are refused by name rather than followed (could send files from outside the selection) or skipped (would send an incomplete tree silently), which also removes the cycle question. Wire: realtime sends populate FileMeta.path exactly as the web does (leaf in name, folder-relative path in path, path absent for a loose file); cloud sends reuse the FROZEN stored manifest by putting the forward-slash relative path in ManifestFile.name — the convention the Go CLI's walkUploadPaths has always emitted and safeJoin has always read — so no new field, no golden-vector change, and old flat manifests are untouched. Receive: ManifestWriter rebuilds safe nested trees for both transports, treating every manifest path as hostile — absolute/traversal/dot/empty segments refused (not repaired), per-segment control+bidi stripping, canonical+case-insensitive duplicate refusal, file-vs-directory prefix refusal, pre-existing target refusal, and cleanup of partial files plus only the directories it created — never the user-chosen parent. The write path is descriptor-relative (openat/mkdirat/fstatat/unlinkat), not path-based: the destination is opened once, every component is walked with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY from the previous component's descriptor, the leaf is taken with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, and the bytes go through the descriptor that call returned — never a reopen by name. The leaf is genuinely single-lookup — O_CREAT|O_EXCL decides and takes the name in one syscall, and every byte afterwards goes through that descriptor. Directory creation does name a component twice (mkdirat then openat); what makes that safe is not a single lookup but exclusive creation plus O_NOFOLLOW on the open, so a swap in between fails the open rather than redirecting it. The property is CONTAINMENT — a lost race is a refusal, never a write outside the destination — not the absence of races. Cleanup of files and subdirectories is confined the same way and uses AT_REMOVEDIR, so 'only while empty' is enforced by the kernel rather than by a losable check. ONE cleanup step is not fully descriptor-relative and is stated exactly rather than glossed: removing the transfer's own container requires naming it in its parent, since macOS has no 'remove the directory this descriptor refers to'. A container this transfer creates is therefore created and PINNED together (createOwnedContainer: mkdirat then openat O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY), the writer takes a dup of that descriptor rather than reopening the path, and every removal compares the name's (st_dev, st_ino) against that ORIGINAL pinned descriptor. Pinning at creation is the load-bearing part: an earlier version opened the container's path inside its own failure handler, which pinned whatever was there at that moment and then compared it against itself — it would have deleted an empty replacement while reading, in review, as a careful identity check. Under ambiguous identity the rule is to LEAK an empty directory (ours, now unreachable by name) rather than delete a replacement. Residual windows, not claimed away: (a) create-to-pin, between mkdirat and openat — a symlink or plain file swapped in there fails the open, but a real DIRECTORY swapped in there does not: it is pinned in place of ours and the transfer writes into it; (b) a swap landing between the identity fstatat and the unlinkat, which at worst removes an attacker's own EMPTY directory (AT_REMOVEDIR refuses a symlink with ENOTDIR and a non-empty directory with ENOTEMPTY, so no data is destroyed). The guarantee is stated as what it is and NOT as containment by location: path lookups cannot be REDIRECTED (a name swapped after its descriptor was opened does not move the operation anchored to it, symlinks fail rather than being followed) and cleanup whose name no longer resolves to the pinned inode leaves that name alone. It is NOT 'nothing lands outside the folder the user chose' — a descriptor pins an inode, not a location, so an actor with write access to the parent can rename the pinned directory anywhere and subsequent writes follow it there; testAPinnedContainerKeepsWorkingAfterItsNameChanges asserts exactly that behaviour rather than pretending otherwise. A folder receive gets its own container named after the sent folder (stepping aside to "name (2)", never merging), with the root lifted out so the tree gains no level; a one-file folder keeps its folder by the same rule. Staged sends are pinned by descriptor: FileURLSource opens each selected file once at staging (O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat-verified regular file) and reads it with pread through that descriptor, so replacing the final component, replacing a directory above it, or substituting a file of exactly the same size between consent and transmission cannot change the bytes sent. The descriptor is owned by a class, so ARC releases it whenever a staged batch is dropped. Every descriptor the receive path holds on a destination or a file in it is close-on-exec, including the container duplicate — dup(2) does not copy FD_CLOEXEC, so that one goes through F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, and a test walks the process's own open descriptors (F_GETPATH) to assert none pointing into a live receive is inheritable by a child process. A completed file is fsync'd before it counts as written and a FAILED sync fails the transfer (errno captured before the close that follows), rather than being swallowed as it briefly was — a full disk must not produce a transfer reported complete whose bytes are not on disk. Retrying a session inherits nothing from the one it replaced: the connection, the SAS, the DataChannel-open flag, any pending receive and its manifest are all released, so a retry must reach readiness on its own two callbacks in either order and cannot install or ACCEPT the previous peer's manifest; the staged OUTBOUND selection and its byte total are deliberately preserved, a partial receive's debris is discarded, and a completed receive's files are kept. A rejected manifest never leaves its container behind, on the cloud multi-flat path as well as the nested one — proved end to end through CloudDownloadModel against a stubbed server, not only on the helper it delegates to. Evidence: FileSelectionTests (22), FolderReceiveTests (26), ManifestWriterRaceTests (18), StagedSourcePinningTests (13), SelectionStoreTests (11), CloudDownloadModelTests (16) + CloudDownloadModelContainerTests (2, one of which downloads a real ciphertext blob end to end and asserts the container and its files), 9 folder/retry/lifecycle cases in RealtimeSessionModelTests, ErrorCopy coverage for every refusal; 573 Swift tests green. The race and pinning tests drive test-only hooks that perform the worst-case swap in the exact syscall window, and are mutation-checked: reverting to reopen-by-path fails 4, dropping O_NOFOLLOW fails 3, dropping O_EXCL fails 3, dropping the regular-file check fails 2, removing the descriptor-owning deinit fails 1, ignoring the fsync result fails 2, removing the container identity check fails 1, leaving SAS/open state across a retry fails 3, leaving the pending receive across a retry fails 3, removing the negative-sum guard reproduces the process trap, reopening the container by path in the cleanup handler fails 2, dropping the identity comparison fails 3, removing BOTH container-cleanup layers fails the end-to-end cloud test, and replacing F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC with a bare dup fails the inheritance test. Interop is pinned by value on both sides: server/internal/cloud/transfer_folder_interop_test.go asserts the same walk order, the same byte-exact manifest JSON, and that a native-shaped folder manifest lands as a real tree in the Go CLI; StoredManifestTests asserts the identical JSON literal. Web consumer fixed to match (DownloadPage splits a slashed name into {name, path}, so a native/CLI folder now reaches the ZIP sink instead of being flattened by per-file blob downloads on Firefox/Safari/mobile). Caveats on the race work specifically: the property is CONTAINMENT — an attacker who wins a race causes a refusal, never a redirect outside the destination — and it does not stop a process that can already write inside the destination, or that can modify a selected file's contents in place through the very inode that was pinned (bounded instead by the per-file chained hash the receiver verifies and by the grown/shrunk-source refusal). Other caveats: an EMPTY directory cannot be sent at all — neither wire format has an entry for a directory — so it is reported in the pane's summary rather than silently dropped; hidden files (.DS_Store) ARE included, matching the Go CLI; backslash is treated as an ordinary Darwin filename character, not a separator, so a name containing one materialises as one inert file here but is split by the web's ZIP sink; the panes themselves are exercised only through their models, and no signed-Release build has been driven by hand

Both directions. Outgoing: NearbyPane + LanDiscoveryModel join the code-less room (STUN-only /api/ice, no mint, no auth, works signed out) and send files or text to a device the user picks by peer id; LanDiscoveryTests/NearbyTransferTests cover self-exclusion, no auto-select, duplicate names, stale selection and TURN exclusion. Incoming: NearbyReceiveModel is composed listener-only on macOS: it observes the discovery room and publishes listening readiness, and answers an unsolicited LEGACY file or text offer with the tagged busy reply a busy Mac sends — before a responder is built — because this target composes neither legacy model. An unsolicited link/1 is admitted through LinkWorkspaceModel.shouldAcceptLink, with the same STUN-only, no-mint, no-token guarantees (RealtimeConnectionFactory.acceptNearby + nearbyICEServers). NearbyReceiveTests/InboundGateTests cover one-session-at-a-time admission, generation-tagged busy replies, buffer-and-replay ordering, exactly-once routing (including a duplicate offer during setup being dropped rather than replayed or refused), glare refusal from the live peer, reservation release on every failure path, a stale attempt from a replaced socket neither building nor reporting over the session that succeeded it, and sequential passive sessions. Live evidence: in-process production E2E (Sources/NearbyReceiveE2E) PASS for file then text against relayium.com, bytes and SAS compared on BOTH sides. Caveats: only advanced verification (off by default) ever establishes who the peer is, and the room is keyed by the server-observed public IP, so anything sharing that address can offer — disclosed in NearbyPane and pausable. Not covered by any automated test: the pane and menu-bar surfaces themselves, which are exercised only through their models

LanDiscoveryModel.startResident keeps one room socket for the life of the process (MenuBarExtra keeps that process up), reconnects on bounded backoff, and honours a sticky user pause. NearbyReceiveModel re-subscribes on every socket via NearbyRoomObserver, so a reconnect does not silently end reachability, and reports off/paused/connecting/reconnecting/active truthfully rather than claiming ready — connecting is distinct because before the hub's welcome this Mac has no peer id and is in nobody's roster. Covered by NearbyReceiveTests (listener follows the socket across a reconnect, a paused listener answers nothing, reconnecting and connecting are reported as such) and LanDiscoveryTests. Current-tree signed Debug QA repeated a live receive after the routing/ownership changes: NearbyReceiveE2E --send-to against the running Relayium.app completed a passive file offer with nothing clicked on the receiving side; the received bytes and hash matched, and the file still existed 55 seconds after completion. That run exposed and drove the fix for a late transport callback deleting an already-completed receive. A signed Release build has never been exercised this way

The Account tab now lists and revokes signed-in devices and lists and deletes stored ciphertext. Server: GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/devices moved from RequireSession to RequireAuth, so the app reaches them with its rlm_cli_ bearer; POST stays session-only because native login already registers a device when it mints that bearer, and widening it would let a leaked token mint device rows. The list response gains one additive field, Current, marking the device that ACTUALLY AUTHENTICATED the request. bearerDeviceID answers that the same way UserFromAuth does or the two disagree about who is calling: UserFromAuth prefers a valid session cookie, so a request carrying both a cookie and a header is a cookie request and marks NO row, while an invalid or expired cookie plus a valid bearer is a bearer request and marks its device. A bearer belonging to another user marks nothing either way. Every other key keeps Go's default capitalization (ID/Name/Kind/CreatedAt/LastSeenAt), which is what MePage.svelte reads today. Ownership is unchanged and still enforced in SQL (id AND user_id), and DELETE keeps answering identically for 'not yours' and 'no such device' rather than gaining an existence leak; deleting a device still cascades its cli_tokens row through the existing FK, which is what makes revoking this Mac end its own session. CSRFGuard is untouched: a cookie DELETE with a foreign Origin is still 403. GET/DELETE /api/files already accepted a bearer and were not changed. Native: AccountManagementModel (RelayiumAppKit) owns every piece of async state — an AccountScope of account id + token is passed into each call and compared on the way out, and loads carry a generation, so a load or an action that lands after a sign-out or a sign-in as somebody else writes nothing, and a revoke invalidates any load already in flight rather than letting its older response resurrect the removed row. Because the model is app-scoped it also has an explicit scope-aware clear(scope:): explicit sign-out and a successful self-revoke drop the leaving account's rows AND the reconstructed #k= links before the ready UI goes, and clearing the active scope is what stops a load or action already in flight from repainting afterwards. The Refresh button no longer reloads blind: AccountRefreshDecision reloads only from a still-ready, same-account session with a nonempty bearer (under the credential the session holds NOW, which a refresh may have rotated) and otherwise clears the old scope, because the view's scope is recomputed from a render-time user plus a live token and can otherwise name an account the session no longer holds. A failed refresh keeps the last known good rows and reports alongside them (AccountSession.isStale's rule); a partial failure still applies the half that succeeded; only the row being acted on is busy or shows an error. Browser rows are filtered out (AccountDevice.holdsRevocableToken) and the rest are ordered by recency with a total tie-break. Identifiers: device and stored-file ids arrive from the server and are composed into a DELETE path, and URL.appendingPathComponent does NOT neutralise them — a direct probe confirms an id of '../me' builds https://host/api/devices/../me with path /api/devices/../me. AccountClient therefore CHECKS the id (StoredLinkKeyValidation.checkedID, the same 1-128 [A-Za-z0-9_-] contract the keychain account name uses) and throws before URLSession sees a request; every id the server can issue here is authx.NewID(), 32 hex characters. The same validation is what keeps a hostile id out of buildDownloadLink, since a link is only built after a key lookup that validated it. Link reconstruction: StoredLinkKeyStore keys each upload's base64url E2E key by opaque stored-file id in the data-protection keychain under the app access group, with the account name namespaced ('stored-link-key:'). Bytes are validated on the way OUT as well as in: decodeLookup turns one SecItemCopyMatching result into an answer, where absent is nil, a refusing keychain is KeychainError, and stored bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or not a usable unpadded base64url key are invalidKey — never nil (which would claim the key is not on this Mac) and never a malformed link. Every Security call runs off the main actor through one helper, asserted rather than assumed. CloudUploadModel and AccountManagementModel share ONE store instance, wired through AppEnvironment and injected as an environment object; the upload persists id->key before presenting the link and, if that write fails, still shows the real link with an explicit warning — never a failed upload, which would invite a retry that sends every byte again. A superseded-but-successful upload still keeps its key, because the bytes reached the server whatever the screen moved on to. The 'Link ready' screen now says exactly ONE thing about the key, chosen in UploadPresentation: on success that the key is stored securely on this Mac and never sent to Relayium's servers (the old fixed 'this link is the only copy of the key' line was false once persistence worked, and contradicted the warning on the failure path), and only on a failed save that the visible link is the only available copy and must be copied now. A file whose key is not here says so and says why, and 'the keychain would not answer' is a third, separately worded state. Every stored-link-key failure the user can read goes through ErrorCopy.storedLinkKeyMessage(for:operation:) rather than the shared copy table, because KeychainError is raised by two stores that mean different things by it: the sign-in token store, where 'macOS wouldn't store your sign-in (keychain error N). You'll stay signed in until you quit' is true, and the per-file key store, where it is false in every clause. That sentence was being rendered verbatim when a file key could not be SAVED after a successful upload, READ while listing the Account tab, or REMOVED after a confirmed delete - telling the user their session was at risk over a file operation that never touched it. Those three paths now say which key operation failed and carry the OSStatus, which is the only diagnosable part (-25308 interaction-not-allowed and -34018 missing-entitlement are different problems with the same symptom) and names nothing about the key or the file. AccountSession keeps the sign-in wording, which is true only for it. Deleting a stored object removes its key only on a CONFIRMED delete: a 404 means the object is almost certainly gone but is also what a failed read on the server looks like, and the two mistakes are not symmetric — an orphaned key is an inert keychain item, while a key destroyed for an object that still exists was the only thing that could ever open it. A confirmed delete whose LOCAL key removal then fails is a third outcome: the row leaves, no row error is raised (the server operation succeeded and there is nothing to retry), and a dismissible non-blocking warning names the file and says the key is still on this Mac and can no longer open anything. Evidence, all observed on this tree: 11 Go tests over the real Routes()/middleware (bearer list and delete, current marking, valid-cookie-beats-same-user-bearer, expired-cookie-falls-through-to-bearer, cookie compatibility, response-shape compatibility, cross-user delete AND rename refused, POST session-only, cross-origin cookie delete still 403, foreign-bearer-with-cookie); 18 AccountClient, 50 model, 18 key-store, 19 CloudUploadModel and 26 ErrorCopy Swift tests; full `swift test` 676 tests, 1 skipped (the opt-in real-keychain round trip in TokenStoreTests) and 0 failures; `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` both re-run from server/ on this final tree after the stored-link-key copy fix and both exited 0, in an independent pass rather than the one that produced the Swift numbers above, with those 11 account handler tests re-run under `-count=1` and all 11 passing; release-readiness validation passed with the live manifest still correctly refused as unapproved; `git diff --check` clean; and an unsigned universal Debug xcodebuild (ARCHS=arm64 x86_64, CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO) that BUILD SUCCEEDED, with `lipo -verify_arch arm64 x86_64` passing on the product binary. Nine mutations were applied to this final tree and all nine were caught: dropping the id check in authedDelete; trusting the bytes the keychain returns; swallowing a key-cleanup failure after a confirmed delete; removing the key on an UNCONFIRMED 404; clearing the rows but keeping the active scope; making clear() ignore which account it was asked for; making Refresh always reload the old scope; restoring the success copy that claims the link is the only copy of the key; and dropping the cookie-precedence guard in bearerDeviceID. Two further mutations were applied after the stored-link-key copy fix and both were caught: routing the save, read and cleanup paths back through the shared copy table (5 tests failed, each printing the borrowed sign-in sentence in place) and dropping the OSStatus from the new copy (4 tests). Caveats, none of them claimed away: the keychain items cannot be exercised under `swift test` at all (a bare SPM host has no keychain-access-groups entitlement), so the two lines that actually call SecItemCopyMatching are the one part no automated test reaches — everything they decide was moved into decodeLookup, which is tested directly — and the real round trip is covered only by the by-hand check in apps/README.md, which has NOT been performed for this change; a signed Debug build and the ready Account surface were inspected by hand, including the 860×560 content floor, but no live-server destructive action was made, so the two confirmation dialogs, stored-link copy path and cleanup-warning state remain exercised only through their models and presentation seams; a hostile stored-file id returned by the upload endpoint would still be interpolated into the displayed link by CloudUploadModel, which fails the key save and warns but does not refuse the link, and was left as-is rather than widening this batch; the reworded strings are exercised through their models and presentation seams, so how the Account tab's own lead sentence and the new detail sentence read together on screen has not been seen; and the WEB device list still filters to Kind == 'cli' (MePage.svelte:79), so devices registered by the native app appear in the Mac app but not on relayium.com/me, which is a pre-existing web-side gap this change deliberately did not widen scope to fix

A signed-in user can start the existing account-deletion flow from the app: AccountView's fourth SectionCard opens a system confirmationDialog whose destructive action calls AccountSession.requestAccountDeletion(), which POSTs /api/account/delete/request with the app's rlm_cli_ bearer. The server route moved from RequireSession to the existing cookie-or-bearer RequireAuth for that one endpoint; the generic accepted response, the per-user+IP rate limit, the email double opt-in and every confirm/purge behaviour are unchanged, and CSRFGuard still rejects a cookie POST carrying a foreign Origin (deletion_bearer_test.go). WHAT THIS IS NOT: requesting deletes nothing. It asks the server to email a confirmation link to the account's own address; only opening that link revokes server-side sessions and device credentials, purges server-stored account data, schedules the hard purge and starts the grace period. The app therefore reports 'requested', never 'deleted', keeps the user signed in until the server revokes the credential on confirmation, and scopes the response to a generation, an account id and the credential so a stale reply cannot repaint a signed-out or replaced account (AccountDeletionRequestTests). BOUNDARY, EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: Apple refresh/access token retention, Apple REST token revocation, daily validation, credential-state observation and Apple server-to-server notifications are NOT implemented (see the deferred note in server/account/apple_native.go). This macOS build carries no Sign in with Apple entitlement at all, so nothing here amounts to Apple account-lifecycle compliance. That work is REQUIRED BEFORE native Sign in with Apple is added to this app, and BEFORE Mac App Store distribution is pursued; it does not gate THIS release, because a Developer ID build handed out directly as a GitHub Release offers no Apple sign-in and therefore holds no Apple credential to retain, revoke, validate or observe.

Drag-in: one FileDropZone and one picker (canChooseDirectories = true) behind all three send flows, replacing the cloud pane's file-only drop and the two realtime panes' folder-rejecting pickers. A drop STAGES and never sends — on NearbyPane the zone sits above and independent of the roster, so a drop cannot pick or dial a device, and sendFiles re-reads the live selection and guards on busy so a second press cannot start duplicate work. Every staging entry point APPENDS with root de-duplication — SelectionStore.add is what a drop, chooseFilesOrFolders, chooseFolders and an OS-opened batch all call, so dropping or choosing the same folder twice is a no-op and a picker cannot silently discard a folder staged ten seconds earlier. The one picker that does not append is chooseForLinkSend, behind Send a link's own two verbs (TransferLinkPane.pick): it builds a FRESH private SelectionStore per press and calls replace(with:) on that, because the batch is a send the user has already committed to rather than staging — which is precisely why it must not write into the surface's shared staged selection. The zone renders but declines while busy rather than vanishing mid-drag. Drag-out: ReceivedResultView offers NSItemProvider(contentsOf:) file URLs for every successfully received realtime and cloud item, built ONLY from receivedPayload, which is only reachable in .completed/.done — i.e. after the writer's finish() returned — so no URL is offered before it is complete and closed. A foldered result offers its container as the single drag item, because dragging the individual files would flatten the tree at the destination. Reveal in Finder is kept on both surfaces and now selects the container for a folder result. Decisions live in RelayiumAppKit (SelectionStore, receivedPayload) and are covered by SelectionStoreTests and FolderReceiveTests' payload cases; the SwiftUI files hold no decisions. Drop decoding accepts every representation public.file-url is actually vended as — Data, URL, NSURL, NSData, String, NSString — rather than only Data, which silently ignored drags from apps that vend an NSURL; non-file URLs and bare paths are rejected, and the result is canonicalised so NSURL's trailing slash for a directory and Data's lack of one cannot stage one folder twice (droppedFileURL, covered by SelectionStoreTests). Sandbox: powerbox issues an implicit process-lifetime extension for picker- and drag-supplied URLs, so staging can enumerate now and open afterwards; readability is not merely probed but HELD — FileURLSource keeps each selected file's descriptor from staging until the batch is released — so an unreadable selection fails before a connection is opened and the staged bytes cannot be swapped while a transfer waits for a peer. Caveats: the drag-out gesture itself and the drop gesture itself are AppKit/SwiftUI surfaces with no automated coverage — only the URL payload seam and the staging decisions behind them are tested — and neither has been exercised by hand in a signed Release build. **1.3.8 (M-1):** drag-in now also reaches Cross-network Transfer and the Device Inbox, which previously required the picker. One reusable adapter does it — admitFileDrop in RelayiumAppKit decides accept/refuse and FileDropReceiver (.acceptsFileDrop) is the SwiftUI seam — so all three surfaces feed the same SelectionStore.add the pickers call and inherit expandSelection, MAX_FILES, the per-path byte limit, the symlink refusal and root de-duplication rather than re-deriving any of them. A drop STAGES on both new surfaces and never sends: Cross-network drops land on the CONNECTED TransferLinkPane (never on the pre-connect pairing screen, which testTheDragDidNotReachEitherPreConnectScreen forbids) and are committed by an explicit link-drop-send with link-drop-clear as the cancellation, gated on link.acceptsWork — the link open AND the SAS answered — re-read at the moment of use rather than trusted from .disabled; Device Inbox drops land in the composer's existing selection, gated on target == nil so a revoked, switched-off or removed device has no drop target, and are still sent by inbox-send-start. Both keyboard-reachable pickers survive on both surfaces. Admission is re-read AFTER the item providers resolve, so a link that ended or a device revoked during the load cannot have the selection written under it. A batch is now admitted WHOLE or not at all: one undecodable item refuses the whole drag with drop.refusedUnreadable instead of silently staging the rest, which is a deliberate tightening of the previous per-item skip. NSItemProvider callbacks are bridged through OneShotClaim, so a drag source that calls its completion handler twice is ignored rather than trapping on a double continuation resume. New copy is English and Simplified Chinese only, per the maintained-language policy. Coverage: FileDropAdmissionTests (30 cases — one file, many files in drop order, folders with hierarchy, every vended payload representation, duplicate drops within and across drags, non-file URLs, bare paths, partial batches, busy precedence, symlink refusal staging nothing, Clear as cancellation, one-shot callbacks under contention, plus the two target-identity families the acceptance review added: a drag resolving across a substituted link attempt or device page is refused as stale with stale outranking both busy and unreadable, a fixed destination never goes stale, and StagedSelectionLifetime's rule that a first report and a repeated same-target report are never substitutions while a replaced device, a new attempt or a return to an earlier target all discard what was staged); MacSurfaceGuardTests and InboxSurfaceGuardTests for the wiring on each surface; LocalSessionUITests asserts the affordance and both pickers on a REAL established cross-network link with no staged batch. Caveats, unchanged in kind: the drag gesture itself is still not automated — XCUITest cannot originate a Finder drag — only the payload seam, the admission decisions and the rendered affordance are covered; and none of this has been exercised by hand in a signed Release build.

Exactly two shipped locales — en and zh-Hans — across the whole macOS UI, matching the web client's LANGS one for one. The clients previously shipped nine; ar, de, es, fr, ja, ko and pt are now FROZEN, preserved with history under apps/localization-archive/frozen-locales/ and outside every build target. Two changes had to land together and neither is sufficient alone: the catalogs MOVED (Package.swift declares .process("Resources") on RelayiumShareKit, which packages every .lproj in that directory, so a catalog left beside en.lproj ships whatever the code says) and AppLanguage LOST the cases (so a Japanese Mac resolves to English rather than to a language with no words behind it). Moving alone would ship seven unselectable catalogs; dropping the cases alone would render raw keys. Boundary: RelayiumShareKit owns the copy and the catalogs (Sources/RelayiumShareKit/Resources/{en,zh-Hans}.lproj/Localizable.strings, resolved through Bundle.module by LocalizationCatalog) so nothing depends on the app's main bundle and the iOS share extension inherits the same strings without linking the transport stack; RelayiumAppKit re-exports the module so every existing import is unchanged. Package.swift declares defaultLocalization "en" and English is the deterministic fallback in code as well. L10nKey/PluralKey are the canonical key list, so a typo'd key does not compile and a catalog entry nothing references fails a test. Every entry point takes an optional explicit AppLanguage, which is what makes an assertion about Chinese wording independent of the machine running it. Declarations: all three Mac bundles (Relayium/Info.plist, RelayiumAppStore/Info.plist, RelayiumShare/Info.plist) declare exactly en and zh-Hans, and knownRegions in Relayium.xcodeproj is (en, Base, zh-Hans). CFBundleLocalizations is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: macOS reads it to decide whether the app is a candidate for a language and how to lay the window out, and App Store Connect reads it to decide which localizations the product page may advertise — so a stale entry is a public claim, not just a runtime one. Fallback behaviour: every archived preference and every regional variant (ja-JP, ar-EG, de-AT, fr-CA, ko-KR, es-MX, pt-BR, ja-Jpan-JP, ar-Arab-EG) resolves to COMPLETE English — asserted key by key against the English catalog, never a raw key — while every Chinese variant (zh, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, zh-Hans-CN, zh-Hant-TW, zh-Hant-HK, zh-Hans-SG) stays Simplified Chinese. Archived GRAMMAR and NUMBERS do not survive either: a French or Portuguese preference gets English's zero-is-plural rule ("0 files ready", not "0 fichier prêt") and a decimal dot rather than the European comma. RTL: no shipped language is right-to-left. AppLanguage.isRightToLeft answers false throughout, and the plumbing that reads it is deliberately kept rather than deleted — both scene roots still derive layoutDirection from the L10n.current resolver and L10n.token still wraps technical values for RTL only, so restoring an RTL language is a one-line change rather than an audit of every screen that prints a path. Today those paths resolve to a left-to-right shell and a verbatim token. Plurals are decided in Swift (PluralRule, CLDR integer rules) rather than in .stringsdict, because stringsdict expansion runs through String.localizedStringWithFormat and would consult the HOST locale — the one thing this layer promises not to do. English has one/other; Chinese has no grammatical number and defines only other.
